body:
jim_customer: Hey team — after the 2026-03-15 deploy our service started returning 401 invalid_api_key for Redwood API calls. Same key works from my laptop curl but fails from the service in staging.

sam_support: Thanks Jim. Can you paste the failing request log (headers + response) from staging? Also which SDK/version?

jim_customer: SDK: ruby-redwood 1.4.2. From staging logs I see the outbound request shows Authorization: [REDACTED] and the response body is {"error":"invalid_api_key"} — weird because we set ENV[REDDIT_API_KEY] (yes, wrong var name in our code initially, sorry ignore that) — we double-checked the right env var and it contains the full key.

dev_ray: Do you have a curl example that works from your laptop? Paste it (please redact for public threads).

jim_customer: Curl that works locally: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_ABC123xyz" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

sam_support: Helpful — thanks. Can someone from infra confirm whether any proxy or edge sanitizer could be rewriting headers?

infra_maya: Noted. I pulled the request from the staging proxy logs (nginx+sidecar). Proxy received header Authorization: [REDACTED] exactly as you saw. That means the client sent the mutated value upstream. Proxy didn't redact it.

dev_ray: Hmm — we rolled out a new logging middleware in the app last night (log-sanitizer v2.1.0). There's a known change where the sanitizer mutates header objects in-place for speed. If code sets req.headers['authorization'] = '[REDACTED]' that will mutate the outgoing request header object. We intended to copy before redacting.

sam_support: Can you show the sanitizer snippet?

dev_ray: Snippet from the version we shipped: 
```
# log_sanitizer.rb (v2.1.0)
headers = request.headers
headers.each do |k, v|
  if sensitive_key?(k)
    headers[k] = '[REDACTED]'
  end
end
log("outgoing", headers)
# -> this mutates request.headers in place
```
Correct behavior should be: 
```
sanitized = request.headers.dup
sanitized.each { |k, v| sanitized[k] = '[REDACTED]' if sensitive_key?(k) }
log("outgoing", sanitized)
```

sam_support: That explains why curl (no sanitizer) worked but staging failed. Any chance the sanitizer got applied to the actual request object in the HTTP client pipeline?

dev_ray: Yes — the middleware runs just before the HTTP client sends the request and uses the same header object. So we redacted the Authorization header that the client then used to call Redwood. Bad.

infra_maya: Repro steps we used: 
1) Deploy a change that requires log sanitization (we used feature flag).
2) Trigger a request that goes through outgoing http client.
3) Observe proxy logs: Authorization: [REDACTED].

sam_support: Nice repro. Jim — sorry for the noise. Root cause is our sanitizer mutating the headers object. Immediate mitigation: disable log-sanitizer feature flag in staging and production until patch is applied.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: rollback feature-flag log-sanitizer -> staging. ETA ~2m. :rocket:

dev_ray: Patch in flight: changed sanitizer to dup headers before mutation and added unit test to ensure original headers unchanged. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/log-sanitizer/pulls/42 (internal).

infra_maya: Confirmed after rollback: requests from staging now show Authorization: Bearer sk_live_ABC123xyz in proxy logs and Redwood responses are 200.

jim_customer: Verified from my side — staging calls working again. Thanks for the quick turnaround. Really appreciate the clear triage. :tada:

sam_support: Postmortem action items: 
- dev: add linter rule / code review checklist to avoid in-place mutation of request objects.
- infra: add an alert if outbound auth headers == "[REDACTED]" to catch this class of issue earlier.
- obs: create a synthetic test that compares local vs staging outbound Authorization header presence post-deploy.

dev_ray: I'll own the sanitizer PR and follow-up tasks. Will add tests + changelog.

sam_support: Closing the support thread for now but will follow up in #postmortems with the full writeup.

jim_customer: Thanks all!
